messages:
maria_ml: Heads up — after rolling v6.0.1 to canary we saw p99 latency jump ~4x on the tokenizer-heavy routes starting at 12:07UTC. No error rate increase, just long tail latency.

alexr: saw that in synthetic traces too. CPU on the host is fine but GPU utilization dropped on the batcher shards. Could be kernel selection fallback.

jin: can we correlate with KV cache hitrate? earlier rollout changed tokenizer prefix handling which might affect prefix cache keys.

maria_ml: good call. KV cache hitrate for the affected model went from ~78% -> ~22% around the same time.

ops_pm: rollout metadata: v6.0.1 includes tokenizer change (subword boundary normalization) + prefetching heuristic tweak. Deployed to 3 canary shards at 12:00UTC.

alexr: attaching a quick profile dump from 12:10 (condensed):
```
Top callers by time:
 - attention_kernel_select (fallback_path): 45%
 - kv_cache_lookup: 20%
 - tokenizer.tokenize_batch: 12%
 - batcher.idle_wait: 10%
```
Looks like kernel-select is spending time probing alternatives after failing fast path.

maria_ml: raw KV profile lines: `kv_gets: 4.1M, kv_hits: 850k, hit_rate: 0.21`

jin: that matches. Tokenizer change increased token splits for many inputs -> different prefixes -> cache miss storm -> more KV lookups -> cache pressure -> evictions. Evictions trigger cold-device execution paths and kernel re-selection because seq-len distribution changed.

ops_pm: is kernel selection probing expensive? Should fallback be more conservative?

alexr: current selection probes a few microkernel candidates to pick best throughput for observed seq-len distribution. But when KV cache misses produce more variable seq lengths mid-request, the runtime sometimes abandons fast vectorized kernels and switches to a more generic fallback that is latency-heavy.

sre_bot: Alert rule perf.p99.v6_canary triggered at 1884012420.

deploy-bot: Rollout paused at 12:16UTC by ops_pm.

maria_ml: quick experiment: rolled v6.0.0 back on one shard and p99 returned to baseline immediately there. So likely regression introduced in v6.0.1.

jin: repro plan: 1) replay representative traffic with tokenizer v6 change in local perf rig; 2) capture KV hit/miss timeline + kernel select traces; 3) try disabling prefetch and test.

alexr: I ran a short replay and saw kernel_select path repeatedly calling `probe_kernel(candidate_id)` with expensive memory ops — wall time increases when probe_count > 2. Our heuristics bump probe_count when seqlen variance > 0.4; the hitstorm artificially increased variance.

maria_ml: suggested immediate mitigations: 1) rollback v6.0.1 on canary (ops already), 2) temporarily reduce kernel probe_count to 1 for canary shards, 3) revert tokenizer prefetch heuristic.

ops_pm: implemented 1 and 2 at 12:22UTC for canary. Monitoring now.

sre_bot: Alert resolved at 1884012540 (p99 back to baseline on canary after changes).

jin: capture notes for root cause: tokenizer change -> more token splits -> decreased KV prefix reuse -> KV cache miss storm -> increased seqlen variance across batches -> kernel-select probed fallback kernels -> increased p99. Also batcher idle/wakeup overhead amplified by smaller cache reuse.

alexr: longer-term fixes to consider: - add cache-key normalization for tokenizer changes - make kernel selection resilient to short-term seqlen variance (sticky selection) - prefetch backoff when cache miss rate spiking - instrument per-request seq-len histogram in traces

maria_ml: added a short perf test to PR checklist to run tokenizer-change replay on staging.

ops_pm: action items assigned: 
 - @alexr to add probe_count circuit breaker (due EOD)
 - @jin to add cache-key normalization proposal for v6.0.2 (due +3 days)
 - @maria_ml to update rollout playbook to include KV-hit sanity check (due tomorrow)

alexr: I pushed a quick change to set probe_count=1 behind feature flag for canary. Logs show kernel_select path time down 60%.

maria_ml: thanks. tagging this thread for postmortem. I'll draft a short summary and link perf artifacts. :memo:

ops_pm: we should also add a test to CI that asserts no >2x p99 regressions on tokenizer-targeted routes when changing tokenization.

jin: agreed. I'll prototype a regression test harness.

sre_bot: Incident closed. Summary: tokenizer-prefetch change in v6.0.1 indirectly caused KV cache misses and kernel selection probes leading to p99 spike. Remediated by rollback + probe_count limiter.

maria_ml: final note — please watch for similar patterns on dedicated clusters; KV miss storms can be noisy-neighbor-like even without noisy tenants.
